newsitem.title: JAPAN: NYMEX Oct crude jumps 22 cents/bbl on missile news.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Oct crude jumps 22 cents/bbl on missile news.

text.p: New York Mercantile Exchange (NYMEX) crude oil prices for October jumped 22 cents per barrel to $23.70 on Tuesday afternoon after the Pentagon said the United States had launched cruise missiles at air defense targets in Iraq, traders said.
The Pentagon said the attack was in retaliation for Iraqi military attacks against Kurds.
NYMEX crude prices trade on an after-hours screen system called ACCESS outside New York trading hours.
The prompt October contract was at $23.48 when the Pentagon released the news of the missile launch around 0558 GMT.
They jumped to $23.70 on the news.
At 0617 GMT, October was last traded at $23.72 per barrel, its highest level since April 22 when the front month traded as high as $24.40.
